article: Why adhesives bond: molecular adhesion and structural joints; all 12 translated editions reviewed by AI
scope: All 12 current translations in this Japanese-source article bundle have AI review records tied to exact source and translation hashes. The concise editions disclose their content-parity limits; batch publication verification remains pending.
findings: Corrected the claim that aircraft such as the 787 are joined exclusively by epoxy films; clarified composite weight fraction, mixed joining methods, process qualification, inspection, and damage tolerance.
Removed categorical claims about epoxy shrinkage, residual stress, creep, and chemical resistance.
Reframed the Dahlquist criterion as an empirical guideline and the fracture path as evidence rather than an automatic pass/fail verdict.
Rewrote surface-energy explanations to include the solid-liquid interfacial energy and avoid unsupported universal energy values/contact angles.
Restored the fracture mechanics, aircraft joining, biomimetic adhesion, and nondestructive inspection/self-healing sections in German.
